title: Staging a Home in California in 2026: New Rules, Real Costs and 3 Local Looks
summary: California's new law asks agents to label staged photos. Learn what to do, what staging costs, and 3 California looks you can stage in minutes.
body_markdown:
## The new rule: say it's staged, and show the original


Since January 1, 2026, a California law called AB 723 asks agents to be open about edited listing photos. Virtual staging is still allowed. You just need to do three things.


1. **Add a short note** on the photo or right next to it, saying it was edited.
2. **Add a link or QR code** to the original photo, and say in the note where to find it.
3. **On your own website or listing page,** show the original photo too, or link to it.


Example note


Virtually staged. See the original photo at yoursite.com/123-main-st


**Apply Design makes step 1 easy.** It can add a "Virtually staged" label right on your photo, plus your own logo as a watermark. You can see the label in the corner of every staged photo in this post. Then just add the link to the original.


### Needs a note


- Adding or removing furniture
- New paint, floors or cabinets
- Changing the yard or outside of the home
- Removing power lines or changing the view


### No note needed


- Brightness and color fixes
- Sharpening
- Cropping or straightening


The law covers homes for sale. Renting one out? Adding the same note is still a good habit.


## What staging really costs


Renting furniture for an empty home costs thousands. Auto Staging costs a few dollars a photo.


### Rented furniture


$4,000 to $6,000


- Days to book and set up
- Rented for 45 to 60 days, then you pay more
- A new look means new furniture


### Apply Design Auto Staging


As low as $7 a photo


- Ready in about 10 minutes
- Yours to keep, no rental clock
- Unlimited changes until you love it


Furniture prices are national averages for an empty home. Ask a local stager for a quote and compare.

## Have an ADU? Show buyers what it can be


Lots of California homes now have a backyard unit or a garage turned into a small home. Empty, it looks like a plain box. Staged, buyers see how they would use it.


- **As a rental:** a cozy bed, a small sofa and a table for two
- **As a home office:** a desk by the window and a few shelves
- **As a place for family:** a comfy bed and a reading chair for parents or grown kids


Stage it two ways and post both. Buyers with different plans will each see their own.


## Your quick checklist


- Take bright, clear photos of every room
- Save the originals before you stage
- Stage each room with Auto Staging
- Add "Virtually staged" and a link to the original
- Show the original on your own listing page
- Stage the ADU more than one way
- Taking more than one photo of a room? The furniture stays the same in every shot


## Questions people ask


Is virtual staging legal in California?


Yes. Since 2026 you just need to say the photo was edited and share the original photo.


Do I need a note for brightness or color fixes?


No. Simple fixes that don't change how the home looks don't need a note.


Does the law cover rentals?


The law is about homes for sale. Adding a note on rental photos is still a good idea.


How much does virtual staging cost with Apply Design?


As low as $7 a photo, and your first photo is free.


This post is general info, not legal advice.[Read the full law (AB 723)](https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/billNavClient.xhtml?bill_id=202520260AB723) or ask your broker.
